speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and have abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. Can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the impact occurred, and have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the rear-end collision and immediate groin pain, was your right leg trapped or compressed between the seat and the steering wheel during the impact? Also, can you pinpoint exactly where the groin pain is located, such as the upper thigh or the inguinal region?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Hip Dislocation.

The specific combination of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a rear-end collision is classic for an anterior hip dislocation, distinguishing it from the externally rotated position seen in posterior dislocations. I am requesting an immediate Hip_XRay to confirm the diagnosis and rule out associated femoral neck fractures.

REQUEST TEST: Hip_XRay
REQUEST IMAGES: Hip_XRay
